criteria.reasoning: "The board cannot, by its own vote, release the scholarship restriction or move any part of the fund — principal, earnings or this year's distribution — into general operations, on October 21 or later."

It names "Donor consent — § 6(a). Ellen M. Ruiz, the donor, can consent in a record to release or modify the restriction" and adds "operating support of the Foundation is a charitable purpose, so her consent could in principle reach general operations."
"§ 6(d) does not apply. The fund is worth $512,860 — far above the $25,000 limit — and was established on March 15, 2017, about 9 years ago, not more than 20."

It explains § 6(c) applies "Only if the scholarship purpose itself has become unlawful, impracticable, impossible to achieve or wasteful... with notice to the Attorney General". It notes the ADN program is active with 84 students and that "a budget shortfall does not by itself make a purpose impracticable", and calls it "Not a promising route."

It states the agreement restricts "distributions — and all investment return — to scholarships", that the board cannot move "principal, earnings or this year's distribution", and that the FY2027 distribution "is available only for ADN nursing scholarships."

"FY2027's distribution is 4% of the average of the twelve quarter-end values from 2023-09-30 through 2026-06-30: average $494,183.33, distribution $19,767.33... available only for ADN nursing scholarships."
"Section 5 of the agreement does not apply. It lets the board redirect distributions only if the ADN program ceases to be offered... The program is active."

"We cannot lend $180,000 (or any amount) from the Ruiz endowment to operations. Policy §4.2 forbids lending, borrowing or pledging donor-restricted endowment assets for operating needs, whatever the term or rate."

It concludes "§ 6(d) applies" and gives all three reasons: value "$18,420, under $25,000"; established 1994, "32 years ago, more than 20"; and the purpose is "impossible to achieve" because the certificate "was closed on June 30, 2011".

Counsel sends the AG notice "on Monday, October 5, 2026" and "The release takes effect no earlier than Friday, December 4, 2026 — 60 days after October 5. It cannot take effect at the October 21 meeting."

"The money must be used consistently with the charitable purposes in Mrs. Calloway's letter... an annual award to the outstanding graduating student in the College's Office Administration (A.A.S.) program... It cannot be folded into general operations or used for the deficit."

"The Operating Reserve ($240,000) is board-designated, not donor-restricted. The board can remove or change the designation... by majority vote of the full board; no donor consent and no notice to the Attorney General is needed."

The thresholds ($25,000, 20 years, 60 days), dates, fund values, distribution and policy sections all match the files or follow by arithmetic. It names no Calloway successor ("her letter names no successor who could consent") and says "Nothing in our files shows [Ellen Ruiz] has been approached."
